definition: The core idea of artificial intelligence systems integration is making individual software components, such as speech synthesizers, interoperable with other components, such as common sense knowledgebases, in order to create larger, broader and more capable A.I.
details: systems. The main methods that have been proposed for integration are message routing, or communication protocols that the software components use to communicate with each other, often through a middleware blackboard system. Most artificial intelligence systems involve some sort of integrated technologies, for example, the integration of speech synthesis technologies with that of speech recognition. However, in recent years, there has been an increasing discussion on the importance of systems integration as a field in its own right. Proponents of this approach are researchers such as Marvin Minsky, Aaron Sloman, Deb Roy, Kristinn R. Thórisson and Michael A. Arbib. A reason for the recent attention A.I. integration is attracting is that there have already been created a number of (relatively) simple A.I. systems for specific problem domains (such as computer vision, speech synthesis, etc.), and that integrating what's already available is a more logical approach to broader A.I. than building monolithic systems from scratch.

explainer.lead: Artificial intelligence systems integration connects specialized AI components so they can work together as a broader, more capable system. It matters because combining existing abilities, such as recognizing speech and reasoning over knowledge, can be more practical than building one enormous system from scratch.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a team where one friend understands spoken words, another knows lots of facts, and another can speak answers aloud. AI systems integration gives them a way to pass messages and share what they know. Together, they can do things none of them could manage alone.
tiers.practitioner: An engineer integrates specialized components through message routing and communication protocols, often using a middleware blackboard for shared exchange. The work centers on making components interoperable rather than rebuilding their individual capabilities. A working connection is only the starting point: the components must exchange useful information for the combined system to become more capable.
tiers.paperLevel: Given specialized components C1, ..., Cn, systems integration defines communication and message-routing mechanisms, potentially mediated by a shared blackboard B, so their capabilities can be composed into a broader AI system. The approach is motivated by the availability of systems for narrow domains such as computer vision and speech synthesis. It is an integration approach rather than a single algorithm, and interoperability alone does not guarantee the desired broader capability.

explainer.example: A speech recognizer turns a spoken question into text and sends it through a blackboard. A common-sense knowledgebase supplies relevant knowledge, and a speech synthesizer turns the resulting answer into spoken words.

usedIn.name: Speech interfaces
usedIn.detail: Speech recognition can be integrated with speech synthesis so a system can both understand spoken input and produce spoken output.

usedIn.name: Broader AI research
usedIn.detail: Existing domain-specific systems, such as computer vision components, can be connected instead of replaced by a monolithic design.

explainer.intuition: A collection of narrow AI abilities can become more useful when the components can exchange information and coordinate their work.
howItWorks: Start with separate components that handle particular tasks.
Give the components communication protocols and route messages between them.
Use middleware, often a blackboard system, to support their exchange of information.
Combine their outputs and abilities to address a broader task.
explainer.whyItMatters: Integration offers a route to broader AI by reusing systems that already work in specific domains. It also makes systems integration a research concern in its own right, not merely an afterthought to component design.
misconceptions: It is not the same as building one monolithic AI system from scratch.
Connecting components does not automatically make them interoperable or the overall system broadly capable.
It is not limited to speech systems; domain-specific technologies such as computer vision can also be integrated.

diagram.caption: Specialized components exchange messages through shared middleware to handle a spoken question.
